A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same POLAR research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–H are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original POLAR experiments on three datasets, including accuracy, efficiency, ablations, transfer, radar-sparsity, and monotonicity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and reports additional ablation and computational-cost comparisons.

M1.justification: The frozen MDE backbone, radar prototypes, aggregation and fusion, polynomial coefficient prediction, and derivative-regularized objective are retained. Direct decoding and alternative aggregation appear as experimental controls, not changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate nuScenes, ZJU-4DRadarCam, and View-of-Delft, including the same transfer and reduced-radar-density scenarios. The ZJU backbone comparison in v3 Table 7 already appeared in v2 Table 9.

E2.justification: TacoDepth with DPT is added to the backbone comparisons on nuScenes and ZJU in v3 Tables 6–7, although TacoDepth already participated in the main benchmarks. The other benchmark comparator sets, including BPNet and NLSPN, are retained.

E3.justification: The reported ablation design changes: v2 tests positional embeddings, whereas v3 specifies replacing feature aggregation with cross-attention and adds a decoder-head control using the fused representation. Main dataset splits, evaluation distances, metrics, and training budget remain unchanged. These additions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 Table 5 replaces the positional-embedding ablation with a feature-aggregation comparison and adds direct decoding to test the benefit of polynomial parameterization. Appendix B adds a backbone-versus-additional-cost breakdown. The degree sweep, transfer, sparsity, regression, and adapter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both Appendix G sections report the same Kendall's tau analysis using 30 bootstrap samples and a two-sample t-test with p = 0.012. No changed seed, repeated-run, or uncertainty-reporting practice is documented.

E6.justification: Changes are concentrated in supporting comparisons; main Tables 1–3 remain identical. POLAR+DPT nuScenes MAE/RMSE changes from 1525.6/3745.0 to 1447.2/3304.9, with other backbone entries also revised. BPNet's 50 m scores change from 2407.0/4438.0 to 1618.9/3596.1, and NLSPN scores change at all three distances. The VoD no-ablation entry changes from 629.6/1171.3 to 1500.1/3951.8, matching Table 1. New ablation results and combined runtime/cost entries are added; reasons for the revised existing scores are not specified.

T1.justification: The method equations, incremental FLOP derivation, and Appendix H proposition, constructive proof, and Taylor-expansion corollary are retained. Notation changes are equivalent; removing the counterexample illustration does not remove its proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about polynomial scene fitting, local monotonicity, accuracy, and efficiency remain unchanged. Both abstracts report average improvements of 24.9% MAE and 33.2% RMSE, and both introductions retain the claim of over 40 fps.

C2.justification: v3 adds the interpretation that superiority over TacoDepth persists with the same DPT backbone and is therefore not solely attributable to backbone choice. It connects the new direct-decoding result to excessive output degrees of freedom and refines the explanation of RadarCam-Depth's structural errors. The stated polynomial-degree and stability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly clarifies that reported inference latency excludes the MDE backbone and provides separate and combined costs in Table 8. This is additional disclosure, not evidence of a changed original timing procedure. Conversely, Section 3.2 drops the explicit definition of temperature tau. Training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al.'s UNCLE depth-completion benchmark citation to Section 2 and develops a focused comparison with TacoDepth concerning backbone choice. The broader research positioning and existing cited works are retained; UNCLE is not introduced as an evaluated baseline.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained with localized editing and simplified notation. Degree sensitivity and ablation discussion move from Appendix A into a new main Section 5, while the ZJU backbone discussion moves from Appendix G to A. Citations change from author-year to numbered style.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout. Figures and tables are resized and relocated, Figures 3–4 exchange numbering, and ablation tables move into the main text. A computational-cost table is added, backbone tables gain comparison highlighting, and the unnumbered Appendix H counterexample plot is removed.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly strengthens the paper through matched-backbone TacoDepth comparisons, a direct-decoding control, correction of the inconsistent VoD ablation entry, and clearer runtime accounting. The central method and benchmark evidence remain stable. A material unresolved issue is that the main text still claims over 40 fps, while the newly disclosed POLAR-plus-Depth-Anything latency is 53.51 ms, approximately 18.7 fps.
